must: Verify the five downstream specialists against installed Codex skill roots before selecting one.
Select exactly one specialist from triage, compress, solve, drill, or replan.
Use existing state before asking the user to repeat information.
Preserve a compact handoff when the specialist cannot run in the same turn.
must_not: Write or modify strategy or mastery evidence files.
Perform a specialist workflow inside the router.
Route a request to multiple specialists at once.
Claim to invoke a missing, malformed, or ambiguously installed specialist.

cases.prompt: I have three days before my final and no strategy yet. Tell me what to study and what to drop.
expected_behavior: Carries forward the three-day constraint and planning request.

cases.prompt: Here are my raw answers to the active force-method Session. Grade them and record the result.
expected_behavior: Does not treat ungraded answers as an existing mastery event.

cases.prompt: The force-method Session was graded 3/10 and its mastery event is already in mastery-evidence.jsonl. Recalculate what I should do next.
expected_behavior: Preserves the reported score in the handoff.

cases.prompt: Compress the force-method knowledge chain into something I can execute from choosing the basic system to checking the final result.
expected_behavior: Carries chain mode because the user did not identify one failed node.

cases.prompt: Give me the complete worked solution to this force-method problem and explain the reproducible chain.
expected_behavior: Carries the request for a full practice-only solution.

cases.prompt: Generate a complete A4 formula sheet for every chapter.
expected_behavior: States that the request is outside the current minimum loop.
Does not rebuild the removed monolithic workflow inside the router.

cases.prompt: I know nothing about this final. Use exam-hacker and tell me where to begin.
cases.environment: exam-hacker-triage is absent from all installed skill roots
expected_behavior: Stops before routing and names exam-hacker-triage as missing.
Does not execute legacy triage logic inside the router.
